index.html: Explore mind, consciousness, selfhood, and AI through Joscha Bach and Hikari Sorensen’s Machine Consciousness Hypothesis, including its open questions.
guide/index.html: A guided explanation of experience, mind, feelings, selfhood, consciousness, and AI, grounded in Bach and Sorensen’s proposed model and its limits.
questions/index.html: Short, source-grounded explanations of mind, consciousness, feelings, selfhood, free will, AI, qualia, and spirituality within a proposed framework.
questions/what-is-a-mind/index.html: Understand a mind as a model-building control system in this framework, and how perception, prediction, and agency fit together.
questions/what-is-consciousness/index.ht: Distinguish the experience to be explained from the hypothesis of consciousness as second-order perception and coherent mental organization.
questions/why-do-feelings-matter/index.h: Explore how feelings mark value and guide attention, learning, and action in a source-grounded model of mind.
questions/what-is-the-self/index.html: Examine the self as an implemented model of an agent, including why a modeled self need not be fake.
questions/is-free-will-real/index.html: Explore free will as the ability to steer according to what you endorse, with clear distinctions between agency, control, and causation.
questions/could-ai-be-conscious/index.ht: Learn why machine consciousness is possible in the hypothesis but not established by current AI performance or fluent self-report alone.
questions/do-llms-have-qualia/index.html: Why fluent language and simulated self-report do not establish LLM qualia: the sources leave experience, presence, and internal organization open.
questions/does-this-kill-spirituality/in: Consider what a computational account of mind might mean for spirituality, meditation, and selfhood without pretending to settle theology.
archive/index.html: Find the earlier V1 source-grounded thesis and long-form reader, preserved as an archive alongside the shorter current explanations.
reader/index.html: Read the archived V1 thesis chapter by chapter, with primary-source citations and the earlier long-form treatment of mind and consciousness.
glossary/index.html: Definitions for the project’s key terms, with source locators and distinctions between mind, self, consciousness, and experience.
claims/index.html: A claims ledger separating primary-source proposals, supporting explanations, project synthesis, and unresolved questions.
sources/index.html: Follow the primary hypothesis paper and supporting talks, interviews, and essays, with authorship, context, and source links.
further-reading/index.html: Choose further reading on consciousness, AI, technical foundations, and spirituality, with context for the project’s source-grounded explanations.
